examples.title: Encyclopedic text
examples.blurb: Names and terms introduced once are copied when they come back.

examples.title: Python code
examples.blurb: Variable and function names are pointed at, not re-generated.

examples.title: Math reasoning
examples.blurb: Intermediate quantities are copied from the problem and from earlier steps.

examples.title: Cumulative rhyme
examples.blurb: A public-domain nursery rhyme where every verse repeats the previous one.

examples.title: Structured data
examples.blurb: Keys are copied; new values fall back to the LM head through the sink.

examples.title: Dialogue
examples.blurb: Speaker names and objects mentioned by one character are picked up by the others.

examples.title: Translation pair
examples.blurb: In the French version, names and numbers are copied from the English one.

examples.title: Server log
examples.blurb: Timestamps, user names and URL paths repeat from line to line.

examples.title: Short story
examples.blurb: Ordinary narrative: copying is occasional, mostly for characters and places.

examples.title: Recipe
examples.blurb: Instructions refer back to ingredients listed at the top.

examples.title: Paper abstract
examples.blurb: Technical prose where the model introduces a term, then reuses it.

examples.title: News article
examples.blurb: A typical news story: names and figures come back once or twice.

examples.title: Long-range recall
examples.blurb: A code is stated, then recalled ~600 tokens later, well beyond the 256-token window of the SW backbone.
